 U.S. Mint Releases $250 Trump Gold Coin, Dollar Bags
 First 24-karat gold proof depicting a sitting U.S. president joins new 1,000-coin bags of Trump dollars
 By Darrin Lee Unser - November 19, 2026 75 
 The United States Mint releases two products featuring President Donald J. Trump today, led by a one-ounce, 24-karat gold proof coin bearing a $250 face value. Joining it are new 1,000-coin bags of the previously issued Trump dollar. Both are part of the Mint’s lineup of coinage marking the nation’s Semiquincentennial, with sales beginning at noon ET.
 US Mint images of the obverse and reverse of the 1776 ~ 2026 W $250 Proof President Donald J Trump Gold Coin 
 Struck at the West Point Mint in .9999 fine gold, the 1776 ~ 2026-W Proof President Trump Gold Coin carries a mintage limit of 75,000 and an introductory price of $4,890.
 It marks the first 24-karat gold proof issued by the Mint to depict a sitting U.S. president, although it is not the first U.S. coin to portray a president while in office. That distinction belongs to the 1926 Sesquicentennial half dollar, which featured President Calvin Coolidge alongside George Washington during celebrations of America’s 150th anniversary.
 2026-W Proof Trump Gold Coin Designs
 First unveiled in September , the $250 gold proof shares its central designs with the Trump dollar, including a portrait of the president on the obverse and the Presidential Seal on the reverse. The gold coin differs in its denomination and precious metal inscriptions and carries a W mint mark identifying West Point production.
 U.S. Mint Chief Engraver Joseph Menna designed the portrait from an official White House photograph by Daniel Torok. Surrounding the likeness are the inscriptions LIBERTY, IN GOD WE TRUST and the dual date 1776 ~ 2026.
 The reverse (tails side) features former U.S. Mint Chief Engraver Frank Gasparro’s Presidential Seal design, depicting an eagle holding an olive branch and a bundle of arrows. A shield covers its breast, while a banner inscribed E PLURIBUS UNUM appears in its beak. Inscribed on the shield is 250 in recognition of the nation’s Semiquincentennial. Additional inscriptions include UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, 1 OZ, .9999 FINE GOLD and 250 DOLLARS.
 Mirror-like fields and finely frosted details distinguish the coin’s proof finish. Each example is encapsulated and housed in a black presentation case bearing the U.S. Mint seal. An outer sleeve displays a gold foil image of the Presidential Seal, and a certificate of authenticity is included.
 Trump $1 Coins Return in 1,000-Coin Bags
 The new 1,000-coin bags offer collectors another way to acquire the dual-dated 1776 ~ 2026 President Trump $1 Coins following their September debut.
 CoinNews photo of 1776 ~ 2026 President Donald J Trump $1 Coin rolls released in September 
 Each bag contains 1,000 circulating-quality coins struck at the Philadelphia Mint. Although produced there, the dollars carry no mint mark. They also have a plain edge and a golden-colored manganese-brass composition containing no gold. Despite their circulating finish, the coins have never entered circulation but remain legal tender.
 Limited to 15,100 bags, the new offering represents up to 15.1 million coins. No household order limit applies, but purchases are restricted to two bags per order because of shipping weight constraints.
 Weighing approximately 20 pounds each, the bags incur an additional shipping fee of $15 for a one-bag order or $30 for a two-bag order. They are made of plastic, have dual handles and measure 14.5 by 25 inches.
 Strong Initial Demand for Trump Dollars
 When Trump dollars first launched Sept. 2 , opening sales reached 49,604 of the 50,000 allotted 100-coin bags and 148,524 of the 150,000 allotted 25-coin rolls. Bags became unavailable in less than an hour, while rolls lasted less than 7 1/2 hours. The September offerings also included 250,000 dollars struck on July 4 with a special JULY 4th privy mark, randomly mixed into rolls and bags.
 Compared with the earlier offerings, the new bulk bags provide a lower price of $1.35 per coin, versus about $1.55 for the 100-coin bags and $2.44 for the 25-coin rolls. Even so, their price represents a 35% premium over the coins’ combined $1,000 face value, before additional shipping costs.
 Trump Gold and Dollar Coin Specifications
 Specification $250 Gold Coin $1 Coin 
 Denomination $250 $1 
 Finish Proof Circulating 
 Composition 99.99% gold 88.5% copper, 6% zinc, 3.5% manganese, 2% nickel 
 Weight 1.000 troy oz. gold 8.100 grams 
 Diameter 32.70 mm 26.49 mm 
 Edge Reeded Plain 
 Mint West Point Philadelphia 
 Mint Mark W None 
 Trump Gold Coin and Dollar Bag Ordering
 Both products become available from the United States Mint beginning at noon ET on Nov. 19:
 2026-W Proof President Donald J. Trump Gold Coin — $4,890; product code 26SQG; mintage limit of 75,000; initial household order limit of four.
 2026 President Donald J. Trump $1 Coin 1,000-Coin Bag — $1,350; product code 26SQBZ; maximum of two bags per order.
 Pricing for the gold coin follows the Mint’s precious-metal pricing schedule and may change with fluctuations in gold prices. Its introductory price of $4,890 is based on a weekly average gold price within the range of $3,850 to $3,899.99 per ounce.
 The Trump gold proof is the Mint’s second $250-denominated coin of 2026, following the 1776 ~ 2026 $250 Freedom Ringing Liberty Bell Gold Coin. Shaped like the Liberty Bell, the one-ounce gold piece debuted July 16 as part of a three-coin release. Limited to 2,026 pieces, it carries a substantially higher price of $19,600.
